functions.description: Convert the prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity percentages into probabilities between 0 and 1
inputs: the prevalence of the disease in the population as a percentage with unit (the fraction of the population that has the disease)
the sensitivity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person with the disease tests positive)
the specificity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person without the disease tests negative)

functions.description: Derive the probability of not having the disease and the false-positive rate from prevalence and specificity.
outputs: probability of not having the disease P(D')

functions.description: Compute the total probability of a positive test by the law of total probability over disease and non-disease groups
inputs: probability of not having the disease P(D')
outputs: total probability of a positive test P(+)

functions.description: Apply Bayes' theorem to obtain the probability of disease given a positive test from sensitivity, prevalence, and total positive probability
inputs: total probability of a positive test P(+)
outputs: posterior probability of disease given a positive test P(D|+)

functions.description: Verify a posterior probability by counting expected true and false positives in a hypothetical population of fixed size.
inputs: posterior probability of disease given a positive test P(D|+)
outputs: fraction of positive results that are true positives

functions.description: Compute the posterior probability of disease given a positive test from prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity percentages.
inputs: the prevalence of the disease in the population as a percentage with unit (the fraction of the population that has the disease)
the sensitivity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person with the disease tests positive)
the specificity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person without the disease tests negative)
outputs: posterior probability of disease given a positive test with base-rate interpretation

entry_points.text: A disease affects ●1 of a population. A test for it has ●2 sensitivity and ●3 specificity. If a randomly chosen person tests positive, what is the probability they actually have the disease?

params.description: the prevalence of the disease in the population as a percentage with unit (the fraction of the population that has the disease)
params.validity_range: Strictly between 0% and 100%. At 0% or 100% the disease is absent or universal, so P(disease | positive) is undefined or trivial. Values must be non-negative.

params.description: the sensitivity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person with the disease tests positive)
params.validity_range: Between 0% and 100% inclusive. Sensitivity of 0% makes P(+) depend only on false positives; the posterior is still defined provided P(+) > 0.

params.description: the specificity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person without the disease tests negative)
params.validity_range: Between 0% and 100% inclusive. Specificity of 100% gives zero false positives; the posterior is undefined only if P(+) = 0, which requires sensitivity 0% together with specificity 100%.
